alignments.note: ἐπισκοποῦντες → 'looking carefully'. Head on 'looking' under rules 91 and 104: the σκοπ- family's English gloss is the verb word 'look', and 'carefully' is the adverbial intensifier the ASV supplies for the ἐπι- prefix. One Greek word to two English words, so rule 2 gives no split.
Ordinary negative/purpose μή rendered 'lest'. Not rule 39's fused cluster: no second particle stands with it.

τις → 'there be any man'. The supplied existential frame rides with the subject indefinite under rule 53's pronoun side: the participle ὑστερῶν is recast as a finite relative and carries its own verb, leaving nothing else in the clause for 'there be'. Rule 11 keeps the ASV's italics from making it 'added'. Rule 17's generic-noun clause heads on 'any' and not on the supplied 'man', as rule 69 heads 'any man' on 'any'.

ὑστερῶν → 'that falleth short'; the relativizer is the participle's helper under rules 7 and 31. Head on 'short' under rule 17's meaning-bearing-complement clause and rule 91's operational test: the ASV pairs this lexeme with a varying light verb (be, fall, come) and an invariant deficiency word (want, behind, short), so the complement is what answers to the lexeme and the verb word is what English idiom varies. Rule 104's contrast does not reach it, ὑστερέω not meaning 'fall' as ἔρχομαι means 'come'. Heading on 'falleth' as the finite lexical verb remains defensible and is the reading this review changed.
ἀπό realized by the English preposition 'of' under rule 36, which gives the preposition to the Greek preposition even where English idiom makes the verb phrasal.
Article aligned to 'the' under rule 19; ἀπό already has its own English preposition, so nothing rides with the article here.
χάριτος → 'grace', a recoverable token pair under rule 26.
Article before θεοῦ, to which the ASV gives no determiner. Rule 23: the article has no 'the' to anchor, and rule 21 forbids leaving a bare 'of' on it, so the case preposition stays with the noun.
θεοῦ → 'of God', the case preposition riding with the noun since the article carries no determiner (rules 21, 23). Head on the noun under rule 17.
Second μή → the repeated 'lest'.
τις → 'any', here attributive to the expressed noun ῥίζα, so no generic completion is in question.
ῥίζα → 'root'.
πικρίας → 'of bitterness'; rule 17 heads a source noun rendered 'of + noun' on the noun. No article stands to take the 'of'.
ἄνω → 'up'; kept separate from the participle under rule 2, the reversal of Greek order being permitted by rule 15.
φύουσα → 'springing'. Split from the adverb under rule 26: both members are independently recoverable, though the ASV's word order reverses them.
ἐνοχλῇ → 'trouble you'. The supplied object is an argument of this verb and stays with it under rule 74's object clause, an ordinary rule 7 pronoun helper; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb.
Expressed καί → 'and', aligned in the ordinary way.

δι᾽ αὐτῆς → 'thereby' is rule 81's named case: 'there-' answers to the pronoun and '-by' to the instrumental preposition, so the pair is one aligned unit headed on the pronominal. Not noncompositional, which rule 45 reserves for an English word answering to neither token.
μιανθῶσιν → 'be defiled'; the passive auxiliary rides with the verb under rule 9 and the head is the lexical verb.

Article aligned to 'the' under rule 19. πολλοί is an expressed adjective the ASV renders by a bare 'many', so the article keeps its own determiner and rule 102's supplied-nominal case does not arise. Variant SBLGNT.HEB.12.15.v008 selected r01, which supplies this article and its adjective; rule 12 keeps the textual decision outside this file.
πολλοί → 'many', split from its article under rule 13.

review_notes: One correction only: the target head of s004 ὑστερῶν moves from 'falleth' (t009) to 'short' (t010). Unit membership, statuses and every other head are unchanged from the accepted alignment.

Reason for that correction: rule 17 names the meaning-bearing complement in support/light-verb and resultative renderings ('make straight' on 'straight', 'bear witness' on 'witness'), and rule 91's operational test asks which English word answers to the lexeme rather than which is the phrase's formal verb. The ASV renders ὑστερέω with an invariant deficiency word and a varying light verb — 'be in want', 'behind', 'come/fall short' — so 'short' is the constant that carries the lexeme. The accepted note's appeal to rule 104's ἐξέρχεται → 'cometh forth' does not carry, because that contrast requires the lexeme's own sense to be the verb word (ἔρχομαι means 'come') and ὑστερέω does not mean 'fall'. The competing reading is named in the unit note, as rule 16 requires.
Partition verified: all 22 source ids and all 30 target ids appear exactly once. Units are now listed in source order (s014 before s015), which was the only other change and is presentational.
s008 remains the sole unrepresented unit — the article before θεοῦ, where the ASV writes a bare 'God' (rules 21, 23). A reference comparison reporting it is not a correction.

The supplied 'there be' (t004, t005) stays folded onto τις rather than marked 'added': rule 53's pronoun side leaves the subject indefinite as the only token in the clause available to carry it, the participle having been recast as its own finite relative with 'that falleth short'. Marking it 'added' under rule 5 was considered and rejected, since a source token does license it (contrast rule 86, where none does).

δι᾽ αὐτῆς → 'thereby' follows rule 81 verbatim and stays aligned. Variant v007 is underdetermined with the base compatible and carries no FALLBACK EXCLUDED mark, so rule 97 is not in play; v008's selection of r01 is a textual decision rule 12 keeps outside this file.
